prompt: The Grafana container is deleted with its volume. What is lost?
hint: Where does each data point live?

choices.text: Every metric, log and trace of the last week
choices.why: Those live in Prometheus, Loki and Jaeger.

choices.text: Its own state: users, settings, unprovisioned dashboards
choices.why: Right. In the lab even the dashboards and data sources come back from files.

choices.text: The Prometheus data source and its history
choices.why: The data source is a pointer; the history is in Prometheus.

choices.text: Nothing, because Grafana keeps a copy inside Prometheus
choices.why: Grafana stores nothing in Prometheus.

prompt: Why does the provisioning file set each data source's `uid` itself?

choices.text: Grafana refuses data sources without a written `uid`
choices.why: It would generate one.

choices.text: So dashboards naming it work on any Grafana that loads the file
choices.why: Right. A generated id exists only on the Grafana that generated it.

choices.text: To hide the data source's address from viewers
choices.why: The `url` is a separate field.

choices.text: Because `uid`s are encrypted and names are not
choices.why: Neither is encrypted.

prompt: In Grafana, a backend it knows how to query, such as Prometheus or Loki, is called a data ___.
The same expression asked through Grafana and of Prometheus gave 5.084 both times. What did Grafana add?
hint: Look at the shape of the answer.

choices.text: A correction for the time zone
choices.why: The value is the same; only the timestamp's unit differs.

choices.text: Only a different format for the answer
choices.why: Right: frames, with the time in milliseconds. Nothing was computed in Grafana.

choices.text: A cache that made it ten times faster
choices.why: Nothing was measured that would say so.

choices.text: Its own estimate, averaged with Prometheus's
choices.why: Grafana computes nothing.

prompt: A dashboard is slow to load. Where is the fix most likely to be?

choices.text: In more memory for the Grafana container
choices.why: Grafana mostly waits on the data sources.

choices.text: In a newer browser
choices.why: Drawing is rarely the slow part.

choices.text: In the queries, or a recording rule
choices.why: Right: a slow dashboard is almost always a slow query.

choices.text: In fewer users allowed to log in
choices.why: That treats the symptom with a policy.

prompt: What should a deploy pipeline use to annotate dashboards?

choices.text: The admin password, stored in the pipeline's variables
choices.why: A leak would give away everything.

choices.text: A service account's token with a small role
choices.why: Right, revocable on its own.

choices.text: An anonymous request, since annotations are harmless
choices.why: Anonymous writes let anybody mark anything.

choices.text: The personal account of whoever set the pipeline up
choices.why: It breaks when that person leaves.

prompt: The robot's token got 200 on the search and 403 on deleting the Prometheus data source. What does the 403 show?

choices.text: That the token had expired
choices.why: The search right before it worked.

choices.text: That the data source did not exist
choices.why: That would be a 404.

choices.text: That its role does not allow it
choices.why: Right. A leaked token cannot remove what every dashboard depends on.

choices.text: That Grafana blocks deletes during business hours
choices.why: There is no such rule.

prompt: What is the main gain of keeping a dashboard as a file in version control?

choices.text: History, review, and a way back
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It loads faster than a clicked one
choices.why: Speed is the same.

choices.text: It needs no data source
choices.why: Every panel still queries one.

choices.text: Grafana can only draw provisioned panels in color
choices.why: Not a thing.

prompt: Saving over the provisioned dashboard through the API returned 400. Why does Grafana refuse?
hint: What would the next reading of the file do?

choices.text: The token lacked the Editor role
choices.why: It was an Editor.

choices.text: The file would undo the edit at the next read
choices.why: Right. Change the file instead.

choices.text: Dashboards cannot be changed once created
choices.why: Unprovisioned ones can.

choices.text: The new title was too short
choices.why: Length was not the problem.

prompt: Put the steps of changing a query on the provisioned dashboard in order.
items: Once merged and deployed, provisioning reloads the file

prompt: Where do the values of the dashboard's `$job` variable come from?
hint: They are not in the file.

choices.text: A list typed into `shop.json`
choices.why: The file has a query, not a list.

choices.text: Prometheus, asked on each load
choices.why: Right: `label_values(...)`.

choices.text: Grafana's user list
choices.why: Users are not jobs.

choices.text: The annotations tagged `deploy`
choices.why: Annotations mark times, not jobs.

prompt: A new service starts next month and publishes `http_server_requests_total`. What must change in the dashboard for it to appear?
hint: Where does the list come from?

choices.text: A new panel per service
choices.why: The variable makes one set of panels serve all.

choices.text: Its name added to the variable's list
choices.why: The list is a query, not a list.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: it appears in `label_values` on its own.

choices.text: A restart of Grafana
choices.why: The query runs on every load.

prompt: What does an annotation on a dashboard record?
hint: The graph shows what the system did.

choices.text: Something people did, at a time
choices.why: Right: a deploy, a change, an incident.

choices.text: A metric too rare to graph
choices.why: Annotations are not metrics.

choices.text: A comment explaining a panel's query
choices.why: That is a panel description.

choices.text: An alert that fired
choices.why: Alerts can be drawn as annotations, but that is not what the deploy marks are.

prompt: The rollback was annotated at 120 s; the p99 line returned to 0.05 s at 180 s. How many seconds did the panel keep showing slow checkouts after they were fast again?
Why did the line stay high for a minute after the rollback?

choices.text: Grafana redraws panels once a minute
choices.why: The data came from Prometheus directly.

choices.text: The rollback took a minute to deploy
choices.why: The fault file was removed at once.

choices.text: Each point is a rate over the minute before it
choices.why: Right, and that minute still held slow checkouts.

choices.text: Payments kept a queue of slow requests
choices.why: There was none.

prompt: The same failures showed as 5.9% over `[1m]` and 1.7% over `[10m]`. Which statement is right?

choices.text: `[10m]` is correct and `[1m]` is noise
choices.why: Both are correct averages over their windows.

choices.text: `[1m]` is correct and `[10m]` is a bug
choices.why: Same answer.

choices.text: Both are true; the panel should say which window
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The difference means some failures were lost
choices.why: The same failures are spread over different periods.

prompt: Which of these make a dashboard mislead? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Drawing missing data as zero
choices.why: Yes: unknown is not zero.

choices.text: A y-axis starting near the values
choices.why: Yes: it turns a small change into a cliff.

choices.text: The mean instead of percentiles
choices.why: Yes: it hides the slow ones.

choices.text: Annotations marking deploys
choices.why: They make a dashboard more honest.

prompt: Match each letter of the RED method to its panel in the shop's dashboard.

pairs.right: Requests per second, by status code

prompt: For a resource such as a disk or a queue, the method's three panels are utilisation, saturation and ___.
During an incident, a teammate says "the rollback did nothing, checkouts are still slow" thirty seconds after it. What do you check first?

choices.text: Whether the rollback deployed the right version
choices.why: Worth checking, after the obvious.

choices.text: The panel's window
choices.why: Right: a one-minute rate still holds the slow minute.

choices.text: Whether Grafana needs restarting
choices.why: Grafana draws what Prometheus answers.

choices.text: Whether the annotation was saved
choices.why: The mark does not change the line.
